intro: Bangkok is one of the easiest cities in the world to meet other solo travelers: hostels, rooftop bars and street-food lanes are full of people exploring on their own. The hard part is finding company for tonight, not in theory.
areas: Rooftop bars, food courts and coworking cafés along the BTS line. Easy to meet after work hours.
The classic backpacker base. Loud, social, and close to the Grand Palace and river piers.
Night markets, rooftop views and the Chao Phraya riverside.
Leafy, local and full of cafés. Popular with digital nomads who stay a few weeks.
plans: Street-food crawl through Chinatown (Yaowarat) after dark
Sunset drinks at a Sukhumvit rooftop bar
Weekend wander around Chatuchak market
Beginner Muay Thai class, then dinner
Chao Phraya boat ride at golden hour
Temple morning at Wat Arun and Wat Pho
safety: Ignore anyone near the Grand Palace who says it's closed today; it's the start of the gem scam.
Book rides in Grab or Bolt instead of haggling with tuk-tuks at night.
Meet new people in busy places and keep an eye on your drink.
best: November to February is the cool, dry season and the busiest for travelers.

hostels.name: Mad Monkey Bangkok
hostels.why: A free Meet Up every evening at 7 pm, a weekly Friday music quiz, and female-only dorms.

hostels.name: Lub d Bangkok Siam
hostels.area: Rama I Road, with a skywalk to BTS National Stadium
hostels.why: Lub d calls it a social hotel. Dorms, common areas and group events.

hostels.name: Lub d Bangkok Chinatown
hostels.area: About 50 m from Sam Yod MRT
hostels.why: Runs a tuk-tuk city tour every Wednesday at 5:30 pm. Yaowarat's night food street is about 1 km away.

meet_spots.name: Khao San Road
meet_spots.why: A 410 m street about 1 km north of the Grand Palace that has been Bangkok's backpacker hub for decades. Bars and street food fill it after dark.

meet_spots.name: Yaowarat Road (Chinatown) at night
meet_spots.why: At night it turns into a large food street that draws tourists and locals.

meet_spots.name: Free walking tours on GuruWalk
meet_spots.why: GuruWalk lists free walking tours with local guides around the Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Chinatown.

intro: Chiang Mai is a digital-nomad favorite: cheap, walkable and slow-paced, with a huge community of people staying for weeks or months. Plans happen daily, from sunrise hikes to night markets.
areas: Cafés, coworking and bars. Where most nomads live and meet.
Temples, guesthouses and the weekend walking streets inside the moat.
Quieter and local, a short ride from Nimman.
plans: Sunday Walking Street market in the Old City
Hike the Monk's Trail up to Wat Pha Lat and Doi Suthep
Thai cooking class with a market visit
Coworking morning in a Nimman café
Swim day at the Grand Canyon water park in Hang Dong
Khao soi lunch crawl
safety: February to April is burning season: air quality can be very poor, so check AQI before outdoor plans.
Scooter crashes are the most common injury; wear a helmet and carry a license.
Temples expect covered shoulders and knees.
best: November to early February: dry, cool and festival season (Yi Peng lanterns in November).

hostels.name: Mad Monkey Chiang Mai
hostels.why: Pool, female-only and mixed dorms, and a free Meet Up at 7 pm every night.

hostels.name: Stamps Backpackers
hostels.why: Pod-style dorms and nightly social events, including BBQ nights and pub crawls.

hostels.name: The Yard Hostel Chiang Mai
hostels.area: Old Town, in a quiet alley
hostels.why: Garden hostel with mixed and female-only dorms and private rooms.

meet_spots.name: Sunday Walking Street
meet_spots.why: Every Sunday from late afternoon (about 4 pm) until about 10 pm in central Chiang Mai, with food stalls inside two temples, Wat Phan On and Wat Sum Pow.

meet_spots.name: Free walking tours on GuruWalk
meet_spots.why: GuruWalk lists free walking tours with local guides, including temple walks and an evening food tour.

meet_spots.name: Nimmanhaemin (Nimman)
meet_spots.why: The cafe and coworking district. A local expat guide says it has the city's strongest meetup scene, with weekly language exchanges, coworking meetups and hiking groups.

intro: Bali attracts solo travelers for surf, yoga and remote work, and most areas have a strong community of people traveling alone. Distances are longer than they look, so meeting people nearby matters.
areas: Surf breaks, cafés, coworking and sunset beach bars. The nomad hub.
Rice terraces, yoga, healthy food and a calmer pace.
Cliffs, surf and beach clubs in the south.
plans: Sunset at Batu Bolong or Echo Beach
Beginner surf lesson in Canggu
Mount Batur sunrise hike
Tegallalang rice terraces and a waterfall day
Morning yoga class in Ubud
Beach club afternoon in Uluwatu
safety: Scooter accidents are common; ride only if you're experienced and insured.
Keep bags and sunglasses away from the monkeys at temples and the Monkey Forest.
Drink bottled or filtered water to avoid 'Bali belly'.
best: April to October is the dry season; July and August are busiest.

hostels.name: Mad Monkey Uluwatu
hostels.why: Pool, bar and restaurant, and a free Meet Up at the bar at 7 pm every night.

hostels.name: The Farm Hostel
hostels.why: Female-only and mixed dorms with privacy curtains, a cafe and hostel events.

meet_spots.name: The Yoga Barn, Ubud
meet_spots.why: Yoga centre with daily classes, ecstatic dance and a garden cafe.

meet_spots.name: Batu Bolong beach, Canggu
meet_spots.why: The beach next to the Batu Bolong temple, with bars and restaurants at the end of the road.

meet_spots.name: Single Fin, Uluwatu
meet_spots.why: Bar and restaurant at Pantai Suluban with a surf check, open until 2 am on Wednesdays and Sundays.

intro: Lisbon is Europe's solo-travel and remote-work capital: sunny, affordable for Western Europe and packed with viewpoints that are made for sharing a drink at sunset.
areas: Tiny bars and street drinking every night. The easiest place to meet people.
Old Lisbon, fado houses and viewpoints.
Riverside nightlife and the Time Out Market.
plans: Sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
Pastel de nata tasting in Belém and Chiado
Fado night in Alfama
Day trip to Sintra's palaces
Surf day at Costa da Caparica
LX Factory brunch and browsing
safety: Pickpockets work Tram 28 and busy viewpoints; keep phones zipped away.
Men offering drugs in Baixa and Bairro Alto are selling fakes; just walk on.
The hills and cobbles are slippery; wear shoes with grip.
best: April to June and September to October: warm without the August crowds.

intro: Mexico City has one of the fastest-growing communities of solo travelers and remote workers, with world-class food, museums and nightlife in walkable neighborhoods.
areas: Cafés, taquerías and bars. The social center for travelers.
Tree-lined streets, parks and dog-friendly cafés.
Colorful, calmer and home to the Frida Kahlo Museum.
plans: Tacos al pastor crawl in Roma and Condesa
Sunrise at the Teotihuacán pyramids
Lucha libre night at Arena México
Frida Kahlo Museum and Coyoacán market
Mezcal bar evening
Sunday bike ride on Paseo de la Reforma
safety: Use Uber or DiDi rather than hailing taxis on the street.
The city is at 2,240 m altitude: go easy on alcohol your first days.
Keep your phone out of sight in crowded Centro streets and the metro.
best: October to April is the dry season; Día de Muertos (early November) is special.

intro: Medellín's spring-like weather, low costs and friendly locals make it a magnet for long-stay travelers. Evenings out are easy to find; going with a group is the smarter way to do it.
areas: Hostels, Parque Lleras and the Provenza nightlife strip.
More local, with good restaurants and cafés.
Quieter, residential and just south of Poblado.
Plaza Botero and museums; visit by day.
plans: Comuna 13 graffiti tour
Day trip to Guatapé and El Peñol rock
Salsa class, then dancing
Metrocable up to Parque Arví
Coffee farm tour outside the city
Provenza bar night
safety: Don't flash phones or jewelry in the street; 'no dar papaya' is the local rule.
Never accept drinks from strangers; drugging (scopolamine) cases are real.
Order taxis through an app, especially at night.
best: Any time of year; December to March is driest.

intro: Barcelona mixes beach, architecture and late nights, and its dinner-at-ten culture makes it easy to join something spontaneous in the evening.
areas: Village feel, plazas full of people every evening.
Tapas bars, cocktail bars and the Picasso Museum.
plans: Tapas and vermut hop in El Born
Sunset at the Bunkers del Carmel
Beach volleyball at Barceloneta
Montjuïc walk and the Magic Fountain
Sagrada Família visit
Sunday flea market and brunch in Poblenou
safety: Barcelona has Europe's most active pickpockets: Las Ramblas, the metro and beaches especially.
Keep bags in front of you on terraces.
Dinner starts late; plan evenings around 9–10 pm.
best: May, June and September: beach weather without the peak crowds.

hostels.name: Generator Barcelona
hostels.why: Its Fiesta Gràcia bar runs karaoke, DJs, live music and social events through the week, with chill-out areas and a lounge to meet people in.

hostels.name: Yeah Hostel Barcelona
hostels.why: A shared living room, a rooftop for sangria with other guests, and group dinners around 9 pm, including a Paella Night.

hostels.name: St Christopher's Inn Barcelona
hostels.area: Carrer de Bergara 3, Eixample, three minutes from Plaça de Catalunya
hostels.why: Belushi's bar downstairs with 25% off food for guests, so there is always someone around in the evening.

meet_spots.name: BCN Languages and Friends language exchanges
meet_spots.why: Weekly language-exchange nights in bars: Wednesday 7 pm at Soda Bus (Aribau 150), Thursday 7 pm at Space Cowboy (Carders 31), Friday 8 pm at Estació de França and Saturday 8 pm pizza night at Trafalgar Pizza Club (Trafalgar 19).

meet_spots.name: Mercat dels Encants
meet_spots.why: Open-air flea market at Castillejos 158, open Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 9 am to 8 pm, with public auctions Monday, Wednesday and Friday 8 to 9 am.

meet_spots.name: Barcelona Casual Runners
meet_spots.why: Group runs on Mondays at 7:30 pm from the Magic Fountain at Plaça de Carles Buïgas (Montjuïc) and Tuesdays at 7:30 pm from La Querida bar, Passeig de Pujades 33, by Ciutadella Park.

women.name: Generator Barcelona
women.why: Lists female-only dorms.

women.name: St Christopher's Inn Barcelona
women.why: Has a female-only floor of dorms.

intro: Tokyo is extremely safe for solo travelers, but it can feel lonely: locals are polite and reserved. Meeting other travelers for an izakaya night or a day hike makes the city far more fun.
areas: The famous crossing, bars and shopping.
Golden Gai's tiny bars and Omoide Yokocho yakitori alleys.
Vintage shops, live music and cafés.
Sensō-ji temple, old Tokyo and budget hostels.
plans: Izakaya hop in Golden Gai or Omoide Yokocho
teamLab digital art museum
Breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market
Karaoke night
Day hike up Mount Takao
Onsen or sento evening
safety: Tokyo is very safe; the main risk is missing the last train (around midnight).
Carry some cash: many small bars and restaurants don't take cards.
Tattoos may be refused in some onsen; check before you go.
best: Late March to early April (cherry blossoms) and October to November.

intro: Buenos Aires runs late: dinner at 10, bars at midnight, dancing until morning. It's a city that is much better with company, and full of travelers staying for weeks.
areas: Bars, parrillas, cafés and most traveler accommodation.
Cobblestones, tango and the Sunday market.
Grand architecture, museums and the famous cemetery.
Up-and-coming, with craft beer and outlet shops.
plans: Asado dinner at a parrilla
Tango milonga (beginner class first)
San Telmo Sunday market
Fútbol match at La Bombonera or El Monumental
Recoleta Cemetery walk
Rooftop drinks in Palermo
safety: Phone snatching is common; don't hold your phone near the curb.
Use official exchange options or cards; ask locals about current rates.
Go to football matches with a tour or a local, not alone.
best: March to May and September to November: mild and lively.

intro: Da Nang has a long beach, mountains next to the city and Hội An 40 minutes away, and it has quickly become one of Southeast Asia's favorite nomad bases.
areas: Beachfront cafés and the expat and traveler hub.
Jungle roads, viewpoints and quiet beaches.
The Dragon Bridge, night markets and rooftop bars.
plans: Sunrise swim and coffee at My Khe
Marble Mountains caves and pagodas
Hải Vân Pass motorbike ride
Lantern night in Hội An old town
Dragon Bridge fire show (weekend nights)
Seafood dinner on the beach
safety: Traffic is the main danger; cross slowly and steadily.
October to December brings heavy rain and typhoons.
Agree prices before rides or use Grab.
best: February to May: dry, warm and not yet scorching.

intro: Berlin is big, creative and international, with a huge population of newcomers. Summer evenings by the canal and weekend nights out are easier with a group.
areas: Canal-side bars, street food and nightlife.
Young, cheap and full of bars and cafés.
Clubs, the East Side Gallery and Boxhagener Platz market.
Museums, history and the main sights.
plans: Picnic and cycling on Tempelhofer Feld
Döner and currywurst crawl
East Side Gallery walk
Mauerpark flea market and Sunday karaoke
Lake day at Schlachtensee or Müggelsee
Techno night (check the dress-down door policy)
safety: Watch the bike lanes; cyclists move fast and have right of way.
Many bars and clubs are cash only.
Club door policies are strict and unpredictable; go in small groups.
best: May to September, when the city lives outdoors.

intro: Cape Town is one of the most beautiful cities on earth, and many of its best experiences, like hikes, road trips and wine tasting, are better (and safer) done with other people.
areas: Bree Street bars and cafés below Table Mountain.
Street art, breweries and the Saturday market.
plans: Lion's Head sunset hike
Table Mountain via Platteklip Gorge or the cable car
Cape Point and the Boulders Beach penguins
Stellenbosch wine tasting day
Surf lesson in Muizenberg
V&A Waterfront evening
safety: Never hike alone; go in a group and start early.
Use Uber at night rather than walking.
Keep valuables out of sight in parked cars.
best: November to March: summer, long days and beach season.

intro: Hanoi is loud, old and full of street food, and its Old Quarter is packed with travelers on their way to Ha Long Bay, Ninh Bình or Sa Pa. Most people stay a few days, so plans come together fast.
areas: Narrow streets, street food, bia hơi corners and most of the hostels. The easiest place to meet people.
The heart of the city. The streets around the lake close to traffic on weekend evenings and fill with people.
Where long-stay travelers and expats live, with lakeside cafés, bars and coworking.
The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the One Pillar Pagoda and quieter, leafy streets.
plans: Street-food walk through the Old Quarter after dark
Bia hơi on plastic stools on Tạ Hiện street
Egg coffee (cà phê trứng) tasting
Water puppet show near Hoàn Kiếm Lake
Day trip to Ninh Bình for Tràng An or Tam Cốc
Group booking for a Ha Long Bay overnight cruise
safety: Traffic is the main danger: cross slowly and steadily and let motorbikes flow around you.
Book rides in Grab or Xanh SM, and agree the price before cyclo or motorbike-taxi trips.
Air quality can be poor, especially in winter; check the AQI before long outdoor plans.
best: October to November and March to April are the most pleasant. Summer is hot, humid and rainy, and winter can be cool and gray.

intro: Seoul is safe, fast and open late, with a subway that goes almost everywhere and a food culture built around sharing. Korean barbecue and fried chicken are made for groups, so it pays to have company.
areas: University area with live music, street performers, bars and lots of hostels.
International restaurants and bars, and plenty of English speakers.
Converted warehouses, cafés, pop-up shops and design studios.
Hanok houses, tea houses and Gyeongbokgung Palace next door.
plans: Korean barbecue and soju dinner
Chimaek (fried chicken and beer) by the Han River
Gyeongbokgung Palace visit (entry is free if you wear hanbok)
Food crawl at Gwangjang Market
Hike Bukhansan for views over the city
Noraebang (karaoke) night in Hongdae
safety: The subway stops running around midnight, so plan your way home; taxis are the usual option after that.
Google Maps has limited directions in Korea; Naver Map or KakaoMap work much better.
Rounds of soju add up quickly at group dinners; pace yourself.
best: April to May for spring blossoms and September to November for fall colors. Summer is hot with a rainy season in July; winter is cold and dry.

intro: Singapore is compact, clean and very safe, and an easy first stop for solo travelers in Southeast Asia. It's also expensive, so sharing hawker tables, rides and tickets with other travelers makes a real difference.
areas: Hawker centers, temples and cocktail bars around Club Street and Ann Siang Hill.
Sultan Mosque, Haji Lane's shops and bars, and Middle Eastern food.
Riverside bars and restaurants; Robertson Quay is the calmer end.
Art deco blocks, bakeries and cafés in one of the oldest housing estates.
plans: Hawker dinner at Maxwell Food Centre or Lau Pa Sat
Evening light show at the Supertree Grove, Gardens by the Bay
Southern Ridges walk across Henderson Waves
Little India and Kampong Glam food walk
Beach afternoon on Sentosa
Sunset walk around Marina Bay
safety: It's very safe, but rules are strictly enforced: no eating or drinking on the MRT, and cross at marked crossings.
Drug laws are among the harshest in the world; never carry anything for anyone.
It's hot and humid all year with sudden afternoon storms; carry water and a small umbrella.
best: Any time: it's warm all year. February to April is usually drier; November to January is the wettest stretch.

intro: Kuala Lumpur is affordable, English-friendly and a popular base for digital nomads, with fast internet, plenty of coworking and some of the best food in Asia. The city is spread out, so most social life happens in a few neighborhoods.
areas: Malls, the Jalan Alor food street and most of the nightlife.
The Petronas Towers, KLCC Park and the high-rise apartments many nomads rent.
Markets, budget hostels and the Kwai Chai Hong lanes.
Cafés, restaurants and bars popular with expats.
plans: Street-food dinner on Jalan Alor
Early trip to Batu Caves, before the heat and crowds
Petronas Towers and the KLCC Park fountain show at night
Rooftop drinks with a view of the towers
Coworking day in Bangsar or KLCC
Morning walk in Perdana Botanical Gardens
safety: Bag snatching from motorbikes happens; carry your bag on the side away from the road.
Use Grab for rides rather than unmetered taxis.
Dress modestly for mosques and temples; the National Mosque lends robes at the door.
best: Any time: it's warm all year. Expect heavy afternoon showers, especially around April and from October to November.

intro: Istanbul spans two continents and could fill weeks: mosques and bazaars, ferries across the Bosphorus and long dinners over meze. It's big and busy, and far more fun with someone to share a table.
areas: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and many budget hotels. Busy by day, quiet at night.
Rooftop bars, meyhanes and the streets around Galata Tower. The social center.
Cafés, galleries and the waterfront by the Galata Bridge.
The Asian side: markets, bars and a local crowd, a short ferry ride from Europe.
plans: Ferry across the Bosphorus to Kadıköy for dinner
Meze and rakı night at a meyhane
Hamam visit
Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar wander
Sunset over the Golden Horn from Galata
Big Turkish breakfast (serpme kahvaltı) on the weekend
safety: Be wary of friendly strangers near Taksim who suggest a bar they know; it's a known scam that ends with a huge bill.
Taxis sometimes take long routes; use an app like BiTaksi and know roughly what the ride should cost.
Dress modestly for mosques; women need to cover their hair, and visits pause at prayer times.
best: April to May and September to October: mild weather and fewer crowds than in summer.

intro: Amsterdam is compact, walkable and very international, with canals, hostels and café terraces that make it easy to meet people. It's also pricey and busy, so a shared plan beats wandering the center alone.
areas: Canals, traditional brown cafés and weekend markets.
The Albert Cuyp Market, cheap eats and busy bars.
Oosterpark, the Dappermarkt and a younger local crowd.
A free ferry ride from Centraal Station to the NDSM wharf, creative spaces and waterside bars.
plans: Bike ride through Vondelpark
Canal boat trip at golden hour
Rijksmuseum or Van Gogh Museum visit (book tickets ahead)
Borrel (after-work drinks) at a brown café
Free ferry to NDSM and dinner in Noord
Day trip to Haarlem or Zaanse Schans
safety: Stay out of the red bike lanes and look both ways; bikes come fast and quietly.
Pickpockets work Centraal Station, trams and busy squares.
Ignore street dealers; what they sell is often fake or dangerous.
best: April to May for tulips and King's Day (late April), and June to September for long evenings outside.

hostels.name: Generator Amsterdam
hostels.area: Mauritskade 57, overlooking Oosterpark, between Centrum and Oost
hostels.why: A former university lecture hall is now the Auditorium bar, open daily until midnight, with DJs, karaoke, live music and pop-up events, plus a terrace and the Oosterbar cocktail basement Thursday to Saturday.

hostels.name: ClinkNOORD
hostels.area: Badhuiskade 3, Amsterdam-Noord, a free ferry from Centraal
hostels.why: Bar open daily 4 pm to midnight and a 24/7 café, with a weekly cinema night, comedy club and DJ night plus beer tastings.

hostels.name: St Christopher's at The Winston
hostels.area: Warmoesstraat 129, one minute from Dam Square
hostels.why: Belushi's bar downstairs has live music, DJs and a garden terrace, an easy place to start a conversation and make plans.

meet_spots.name: Language Exchange Bar Nights at Pacific
meet_spots.why: A language-exchange evening usually on the first Thursday of the month, 7:30 to 10:30 pm, at Pacific in Westerpark (Polonceaukade 23); the next one is Thursday 5 November.

meet_spots.name: Noordermarkt
meet_spots.why: Market on the square in front of the Noorderkerk in the Jordaan, Saturday 9 am to 4 pm and Monday 9 am to 2 pm.

meet_spots.name: Sandemans free tour of Amsterdam
meet_spots.why: A tips-based walking tour of about two hours that starts in front of the National Monument on Dam Square, a simple way to spend a morning with other travelers.

women.name: Generator Amsterdam
women.why: Lists female-only dorms, including a 6-bed women-only room.

women.name: ClinkNOORD
women.why: Has en-suite female-only dorms sleeping 4 to 10.

intro: Prague has a beautiful old center, beer that's cheap by Western European standards and a big hostel scene, so it's easy to meet other travelers. A few tram stops out, it feels far more local.
areas: Charles Bridge, Old Town Square and the castle hill. Stunning, and very crowded.
Wine bars, cafés and the Riegrovy sady beer garden with sunset views.
Lots of pubs, the TV Tower and a relaxed, local feel.
Galleries, the DOX art center and the Letná beer garden nearby.
plans: Sunset beers at the Letná beer garden
Early-morning walk over Charles Bridge before the crowds
Prague Castle and a walk down through Petřín hill
Czech pub dinner: goulash, dumplings and a pilsner
Saturday farmers' market on the Náplavka riverbank
Day trip to Kutná Hora or Český Krumlov
safety: Skip exchange booths advertising 'no commission'; use bank ATMs and decline the machine's currency conversion.
Use Bolt, Uber or a booked taxi rather than cabs waiting at tourist spots.
Pickpockets work Old Town Square, the Astronomical Clock crowd and busy trams.
best: May to June and September: warm and green. December brings the Christmas markets.

intro: Cusco is the gateway to Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley, and almost everyone in town is getting ready for a trek. That makes it one of the easiest places in South America to find travel companions.
areas: Steep lanes, artisan workshops, cafés and small bars.
The cathedral, restaurants and most of the tour agencies.
Cheap lunches, fresh juice and everyday local life.
Lower, quieter towns about an hour or two away.
plans: Machu Picchu trip (entry tickets sell out, so book ahead)
Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca) day hike
Sacred Valley day: Pisac, Moray and Ollantaytambo
Lunch and juice at San Pedro Market
Find a group for the Salkantay or Inca Trail trek
Walk up to the Sacsayhuamán ruins
safety: Cusco sits at about 3,400 m: take it slow for the first day or two, drink water and go easy on alcohol.
The Inca Trail can only be hiked with a licensed operator; for any trek, choose well-reviewed agencies.
At night, use official taxis or a ride app rather than unmarked cars.
best: May to September is the dry season and the best time to trek. The Inca Trail closes every February for maintenance.

intro: Paris rewards wandering on your own, but long dinners and wine by the Seine are better shared. Plenty of travelers pass through alone, and its cafés make lingering normal.
areas: Galleries, falafel on Rue des Rosiers and busy bars.
Picnics and drinks along the canal on warm evenings.
Sacré-Cœur, views and village streets; very busy with visitors.
Students, bookshops and cheap eats near the Sorbonne.
plans: Picnic and wine on the banks of the Seine at sunset
Louvre or Musée d'Orsay morning, then lunch
Sunset on the steps of Sacré-Cœur
Bar hop in Le Marais
Day trip to Versailles
Market morning at the Marché des Enfants Rouges
safety: Pickpockets work the metro and the crowds around the Eiffel Tower and Sacré-Cœur.
Walk past anyone asking you to sign a petition or tying a 'friendship bracelet' on your wrist; both are scams.
Keep your phone off café tables next to the street.
best: April to June and September to October, when it's mild and less crowded than summer.

intro: London is huge and can feel anonymous, but it's full of newcomers, pubs and free museums. Company is easy to find once you make a plan.
areas: Street art, bars and curry and bagels on Brick Lane.
Markets, live music and canal walks.
The riverside walk, Borough Market and theaters.
Pubs, restaurants and West End shows.
plans: Pub quiz night
Borough Market lunch and a South Bank walk
Free museum afternoon at the British Museum or Tate Modern
Sunday roast in a pub
Camden Market and a Regent's Canal walk
Cheap day-of tickets for a West End show
safety: Phone snatching by thieves on bikes and mopeds happens; keep your phone away from the curb.
Take licensed black cabs or app rides, never an unbooked minicab.
Watch your bag on crowded Tube lines and at markets.
best: May to September for long evenings; museums and pubs work all year.

intro: New York moves fast and nobody minds you being on your own, at a counter seat or a bar stool. It's also expensive, so splitting plans with other travelers helps.
areas: Bars, cheap eats and late nights.
Jazz clubs, comedy cellars and Washington Square Park.
The big sights, Broadway and the south end of Central Park.
plans: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge at sunset
Comedy show in Greenwich Village
Pizza slice crawl
Free Staten Island Ferry ride past the Statue of Liberty
Picnic in Central Park
Weekend food market in Brooklyn
safety: Costumed characters in Times Square expect money after a photo; agree or walk on.
Late at night, ride in a subway car with other passengers in it.
Tipping 18 to 20% is expected at restaurants and bars, so budget for it when you split a bill.
best: April to June and September to November; summers are hot and winters cold.

intro: Madrid eats late and goes out later. Tapas crawls and terraces are made for groups, and the city is used to newcomers joining in.
areas: Tapas bars on Cava Baja and Sunday crowds after El Rastro market.
Indie bars, vintage shops and cheap drinks.
Multicultural, with cheap eats and rooftop terraces.
The big park and the city's major art museums.
plans: Tapas crawl on Cava Baja
El Rastro flea market on Sunday morning
Rowing boats on the Retiro lake
The Prado in its free-entry evening hours
Sunset at the Templo de Debod
Day trip to Toledo or Segovia
safety: Pickpockets work Puerta del Sol, the metro and El Rastro.
Keep bags on your lap on terraces; snatching from chair backs happens.
Dinner starts around 9pm or later, so plan meetups late.
best: April to June and September to October; July and August are very hot.

intro: Rome is a city for long walks and longer dinners. Aperitivo hour and the evening stroll make it easy to fall in with other people.
areas: Cobbled lanes, trattorias and the busiest nightlife.
Wine bars and small shops near the Colosseum.
The Pantheon, Piazza Navona and gelato stops.
A local food market and traditional Roman cooking.
plans: Aperitivo in Trastevere
Colosseum and Roman Forum morning

intro: Rio mixes beach days, samba and mountain views. It's social and friendly, and it's also a city where going out in a group is the sensible choice.
areas: Beach life, sunset at Arpoador and good restaurants.
The famous beach, big hotels and beach kiosks.
Bars, craft beer and views of Sugarloaf.
Samba nights under the arches, and a hilltop arts neighborhood.

Samba night in Lapa
Hike to the Dois Irmãos viewpoint

Early visit to Christ the Redeemer before the crowds

Use app rides at night instead of walking.
Only visit favelas with a reputable local guide.
best: May to October is drier and less hot; Carnival in February or March is the biggest party of the year.

intro: Dubai is spread out and built around cars and malls. Brunches, desert trips and beach days are all more fun with a group.
areas: A beach walk, restaurants and waterfront bars.
The Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall and the fountain shows.
Old Dubai, the souks and abra boat rides across the creek.
Public beaches, cafés and La Mer.

Abra ride and a souk walk in Deira
Weekend brunch
Sunset at Kite Beach
Burj Khalifa observation deck at sunset
Evening walk around the Dubai Fountain

Dress modestly in the old town, souks and malls.
Some medicines that are legal at home are controlled in the UAE; check before you fly.
best: November to March; summer temperatures regularly pass 40°C.

intro: Valencia has beaches, paella and a long park in an old riverbed, and it's become a favorite base for digital nomads. It's relaxed, flat and easy to cycle.
areas: Cafés, coworking spaces and the liveliest bars.
The old town's lanes, street art and late nights.
The old fishermen's quarter by the beach.
A student area with cheap bars and a local feel.

Use the bike lanes; the Valenbisi bike share makes cycling easy.
Book early for Las Fallas in March, when prices jump.
best: March to June and September to November; Las Fallas fills the city in mid-March.

intro: Koh Phangan is known for the Full Moon Party, but it also has a big community of yoga people and digital nomads who stay for weeks. Social life happens at cafés, beaches and sunset spots.
areas: The Full Moon Party beach; loud and busy.
Yoga schools, vegan cafés and long-stay nomads.
The main town and pier, with a weekend walking street market.
Quieter west coast beaches with sunsets.

At the Full Moon Party, leave valuables behind and watch your drink.
Thai drug laws are strict.

intro: Budapest is compact, affordable and known for ruin bars and thermal baths. Hostels here are social, and nights out are easy to join.
areas: Ruin bars like Szimpla Kert and most of the nightlife.
The Danube promenade, Parliament and the main sights.
Buda Castle, Fisherman's Bastion and the views.
Up-and-coming, with cheaper bars and cafés.

Afternoon at the Széchenyi thermal baths
Sunset at Fisherman's Bastion
Evening cruise on the Danube

Don't follow friendly strangers to a bar they pick; huge bills are a known scam.
Hungary uses the forint, and street exchange rates vary a lot.

intro: Ho Chi Minh City, still called Saigon by most people, runs on motorbikes, street food and coffee. It's easy to meet people over a plastic-stool dinner.
areas: Bui Vien walking street, the main sights and nightlife.
Local cafés, street food and quieter streets.
Expats and nomads, cafés and coworking spaces.
Seafood and street food near the river.

Day trip to the Cu Chi tunnels
Mekong Delta day trip
Rooftop drinks in District 1
Coffee crawl: try egg coffee and coconut coffee
Lunch at Ben Thanh market

Book rides in Grab or another ride-hailing app.

intro: Goa is India's beach state, with a slow pace, Portuguese heritage and a big backpacker and nomad scene in the north. Beach shacks and sunset spots make meeting people easy.
areas: Cliffs, beach shacks, the Wednesday flea market and nightlife.
Bohemian, with sunset drum circles and long-stay travelers.
The capital, with the old Latin Quarter of Fontainhas.
A calmer crescent beach in South Goa, good for kayaking.

Wednesday flea market in Anjuna
Scooter day along the northern beaches
Walk through the Fontainhas Latin Quarter

Sea currents get strong, especially in the monsoon; swim where lifeguards are posted.

areas: Cafés, yoga schools and guesthouses popular with travelers.
Cafés and river views around the old bridge.
The evening Ganga aarti ceremony by the river.

intro: Manali is the Himalayan base for Himachal Pradesh: cafés and guesthouses in Old Manali, hot springs in Vashisht and treks, snow and paragliding up the valley. Most travelers arrive on an overnight bus from Delhi, so there's always someone new in town looking for company.

A village across the river with natural hot springs, cafés and the trail to Jogini Falls.
The main market in town: shops, food and the bus stand. Busy with domestic tourists.
The wooden Hadimba Devi temple in a cedar forest, a short walk from Old Manali.

best: March to June for mild weather, and October to November for clear skies; December to February brings snow, and the July to August monsoon brings landslides.

intro: Kasol is a small village on the Parvati river and the gateway to the Parvati Valley's treks and hamlets. It's one of the most popular stops for backpackers in Himachal Pradesh, and café tables and trailheads make it easy to fall in with a group.

safety: Foreign tourists have gone missing in and around the Parvati Valley since the early 1990s, according to Wikipedia. The UK government's travel advice says trekkers should travel in groups, use reputable local guides, stay on established routes and leave their plans with their accommodation.
The Parvati river is fast and freezing; don't swim in it.

Charas and ganja (cannabis resin and flowers) are illegal in India, including in the Parvati Valley, which is known for locally grown cannabis. The UK government's travel advice says possession of a small amount for personal use could mean at least 6 months in prison.
tips: Overnight buses from Delhi go to Bhuntar; from there it's about an hour by local bus or taxi.
Mobile signal and ATMs are patchy further up the valley, so carry some cash.

best: March to June and September to November; winters are cold and the July to August monsoon brings landslides.

intro: Leh is the capital of Ladakh, at about 3,500 m, and the starting point for Pangong Tso, Nubra Valley and the high passes. Sharing taxis and bikes to far-away lakes is part of traveling here, so finding other travelers for a trip is genuinely useful.
areas: The market, cafés, bakeries and travel agents in the center of town.
Guesthouses, cafés and the road up to the Shanti Stupa.
Restaurants, gear shops and taxi and bike rental.
plans: Sunset at Shanti Stupa

safety: Altitude sickness is the main risk: rest for at least two days after you arrive, especially if you fly in, drink water and skip alcohol at first.

Pangong, Nubra and Tso Moriri are protected areas: foreign visitors need a Protected Area Permit, and Indian visitors should check the current rules and fees before setting off. Agents in Leh can arrange permits.
Medical help is limited outside Leh, so don't drive or ride the high passes alone.
tips: Shared taxis are cheaper when the seats are full, which is exactly the kind of plan to post.
Check your mobile network before you go; not every connection from other states works in Ladakh.
Nights are cold even in July, and the sun is strong at this altitude.
best: May to September, when the roads over the passes are usually open; winters are extremely cold and many guesthouses close.

extra.title: Finding people to share a taxi
extra.intro: Ladakh's taxi fares are per vehicle, so solo travelers save a lot by filling a shared taxi for the trips out of Leh. What we could check on 11 October 2026:

items.name: Only Ladakh taxis do sightseeing
items.why: The Ladakh Taxi Union publishes the fares each season, and taxis from outside Ladakh can't be used for sightseeing inside it. A Ladakh travel guide updated in October 2026 gives ₹10,470 for a one-day Pangong Tso trip in an Innova on the current rate card, which is why filling the seats matters.

items.name: Where seats are found
items.why: The main Leh taxi stand, cafés on Fort Road and Changspa Road, and notice boards at restaurants and guesthouses, where solo travelers pin up flyers looking for people to share a taxi. Travel agents also sell single seats on shared taxi trips, for about ₹200 to ₹300 more a person, according to the same guide.

items.name: An online shared-taxi board
items.why: On lehladakhtaxis.com, one group posts a tour and a date and another group asks to join. Neither card is charged until both groups confirm, within 3 days. It showed no open ads on 11 October, after the main season.

items.name: The busiest months
items.why: The same guide puts Ladakh's taxi season at June to September, with July and August the peak, and says the passes to Nubra and Pangong usually open by mid-June. More travelers in town means seats fill faster.

faq: How do I find people to share a taxi in Ladakh?

In Leh, ask at the main taxi stand, read the flyers in cafés on Fort Road and Changspa Road and at guesthouses, ask your hostel, or post on an online shared-taxi board. Travel agents also sell single seats for a little more. On Tablamigo you can post a plan such as "Taxi to Pangong on Friday, 2 seats left" for travelers nearby to join.

Evening Ganga aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat

intro: Jaipur, Rajasthan's Pink City, packs forts, palaces and bazaars into a city that's easy to reach from Delhi. Sightseeing days are long and hot, so they're more fun shared, and splitting a car to Amer or Nahargarh saves money too.

Cafés, restaurants and bars in the newer city.
Guesthouses and hostels a short ride from the station and the old city.

tips: A composite ticket covers several monuments and saves money if you see more than two.

intro: Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka: the ruins of the Vijayanagara capital spread across a landscape of giant boulders and banana fields. Travelers explore by bicycle or scooter and meet up again at sunset on the hills.
areas: The area around the Virupaksha Temple, with guesthouses and cafés close to the ruins.
Across the Tungabhadra river. Many of the old backpacker guesthouses at Virupapur Gaddi have closed or moved; Sanapura, about 3 km west, has huts and shacks in the same spirit.
A village at the southern end of the site, near the Royal Enclosure.
An older village across the river with a slower pace.

Coracle ride on the Tungabhadra
Bouldering session across the river
Cycle between the ruins for a day
safety: The river ferry stops when the water is high in the monsoon; check before you cross late in the day.
Climb Matanga Hill for sunrise with other people, not alone in the dark.
Carry water and sun protection; there's little shade between the ruins.
tips: The nearest railway station is Hosapete (Hospet), about 13 km away.
Rent a bicycle or scooter; the site is too spread out to walk in a day.
Many guesthouses across the river close in the summer and monsoon months.
best: October to February; March to May is very hot.

intro: Delhi is where many trips around India begin: Mughal monuments, Old Delhi's food lanes and a metro that makes the city easy to cross. It's big and busy, so a few days with other travelers is a gentle start before heading to the mountains or Rajasthan.
areas: Budget hotels and hostels next to New Delhi railway station.
Bars, cafés and a lake beside medieval ruins in south Delhi.
The Tibetan colony in north Delhi, with cafés and momos, and buses to the mountains.
Jama Masjid, the Red Fort and the city's most famous street food.

Qutub Minar visit
safety: At New Delhi railway station, ignore anyone who says your ticket or hotel is invalid and offers to take you to a 'tourist office'.
Use the metro or ride-hailing apps; the first coach of every metro train is for women only.
Air quality is often very poor from late October to January; check the AQI before outdoor plans.
tips: Buy a metro smart card or use a QR ticket; the Airport Express line reaches the city from the airport.
Stay near a metro station to save hours in traffic.
Majnu ka Tilla is where many overnight buses to Manali, Kasol and McLeod Ganj leave from, which makes it a good place to find travel companions heading north.
best: October to March; April to June is very hot, and smog peaks from November to January.

description: Traveling solo in Spiti Valley? Where travelers meet in Kaza, plans to share a cab, safety and altitude tips and the best time to go.
intro: Spiti is a high, cold desert valley in Himachal Pradesh, and Kaza, at about 3,650 m, is its main town and the base for most trips. Unlike Leh, Spiti has few tourist shared taxis, so finding other travelers to split a cab to the villages is the main practical reason to meet people here.
areas: The bus stand, cafés, guesthouses and taxi drivers. Nearly every trip in Spiti starts or ends here.
Villages above Kaza: Key Monastery on its hilltop, and Kibber, 19 km from Kaza, by the Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary.
High villages on a loop above Kaza, with Langza's fossils, Hikkim's post office and Komic's monastery.
A side valley with its own villages, reached by the daily bus from Kaza to Mudh.
plans: Share a taxi from Kaza to Key Monastery, Kibber and Chicham
The Langza, Hikkim and Komic loop: fossils, the post office and a monastery
A day trip into Pin Valley
Dhankar and Tabo on the way out towards Shimla
Chandratal on the way to or from Manali, while the road is open
Chai in Kaza market after a day out
safety: Altitude is the main risk: Kaza is at about 3,650 m and the villages above it are higher still. Coming up through Shimla and Kinnaur lets your body adjust; rest when you arrive and don't rush to the high points.
Carry enough cash: Kaza's SBI ATM is often out of service, especially in winter. Fuel is sold at Reckong Peo, Tabo and Kaza.
Mobile signal is patchy. BSNL postpaid has the widest coverage, and Jio and Airtel have little or none in most of Spiti.
Travel the mountain roads in daylight, check the road status before crossing the Kunzum Pass, and don't drive or ride alone.
tips: Village buses from Kaza leave in the late afternoon and come back the next morning, so a day trip by bus means staying the night. That's why travelers share taxis for day trips.
Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit for upper Kinnaur, around Nako and Pooh, on the Shimla road; Indian citizens don't.
best: June to mid-October, when both roads are usually open, with September often the clearest month. Winters are severe.

meet_spots.name: Kaza market
meet_spots.why: Spiti's largest town and the place almost every traveler passes through, split into the old Kaza Khas and the newer Kaza Soma.

meet_spots.name: Key Monastery
meet_spots.why: The largest monastery in Spiti, a Gelugpa monastery on a hilltop at about 4,166 m close to the Spiti River.

meet_spots.name: Hikkim post office
meet_spots.why: One of the highest post offices in the world, at about 4,400 m, with the same postmaster since it opened in 1983. Travelers come to send postcards; it shuts in winter.

meet_spots.name: Langza
meet_spots.why: A village of about 136 people below Chau Chau Kang Nilda, known as Spiti's fossil village.

meet_spots.name: Chandratal
meet_spots.why: A crescent-shaped lake at about 4,300 m on the Manali side, reached by road from Batal or on foot from the Kunzum Pass between late May and early October. The last 1 km from the car park is on foot.

women.name: Jugni, a women-only travel group
women.why: Names Spiti among its regular domestic trips, alongside Ladakh, Meghalaya and Kerala, in its FAQ.

extra.title: Sharing taxis and buses out of Kaza
extra.intro: This is the main reason to find other travelers in Spiti. What we could check on 11 October 2026:

items.name: Tourist shared taxis are scarce
items.why: Unlike in Leh, you don't easily find tourist shared taxis in Spiti, says a Spiti public-transport guide updated in August 2026. Local shared taxis run from one village to the next without sightseeing stops, so a day out usually means filling a taxi yourself.

items.name: Village buses run overnight
items.why: The same guide lists daily HRTC buses from Kaza to Mudh in Pin Valley (4 pm), Losar (4:30 pm), Komic (5 pm) and Chicham (5:15 pm), each coming back the next morning.

items.name: Permits for foreign visitors
items.why: Kinnaur district says no foreigner can enter or stay in the state's protected area, which includes Nako and Pooh on the Shimla road, without a permit, and that foreign tourists in groups of two or more sponsored by a recognised travel agency can be allowed in for 30 days.

extra.title: Where to stay in Spiti
extra.intro: We found few hostels in Spiti; most travelers stay in guesthouses and homestays. What Hostelworld and Zostel listed on 11 October 2026:

items.name: Hostelworld's Kaza listing
items.why: Showed one property: Piti Khangpa, a guesthouse with dorms in Rangrik, about 6 km from Kaza.

items.name: Zostel Homes Tabo
items.why: A Zostel homestay near the Tabo Monastery with a common area and private rooms. Zostel's Spiti page also lists Zostel Sissu, which is in Lahaul on the Manali road, not in Spiti.

getting_there.name: From Delhi via Shimla
getting_there.why: The Shimla and Kinnaur road is open all year, though winter driving is hard. There's no direct bus from Shimla to Kaza: take a bus to Reckong Peo, then the daily 7 am bus to Kaza.

getting_there.name: From Manali
getting_there.why: The road through the Atal Tunnel and over the Kunzum Pass (4,551 m) usually opens between late May and mid-June and closes in late October or early November, depending on snow.

getting_there.name: Group trips from Delhi
getting_there.why: Zostel's Zo Trips listed a Spiti winter trip from Delhi with departures from 16 October 2026.

faq: Can I share a taxi in Spiti?

Yes, but you usually have to find the other passengers yourself. Tourist shared taxis are hard to find in Spiti, unlike in Leh, and local shared taxis don't stop for sightseeing. Ask at your guesthouse and in Kaza market, or post a plan on Tablamigo, such as "Taxi to Key, Kibber and Chicham tomorrow at 9, 3 seats".
Do I need a permit for Spiti?

Indian citizens don't. Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit for upper Kinnaur, around Nako and Pooh on the Shimla road; Kinnaur district allows foreign tourists in groups of two or more sponsored by a recognised travel agency.

description: Traveling solo in Gokarna? Where travelers meet, social hostels by the beach, plans to join, safety tips and the best time to go.
intro: Gokarna is a temple town on the Karnataka coast, about 125 km south of Madgaon in Goa. The Mahabaleshwar Temple is in town, and a run of beaches stretches south of it: Main Beach, Kudle, Om, Half Moon and Paradise. Walking from one beach to the next is the obvious thing to do with company.
areas: The temple town, with the Mahabaleshwar Temple, the market and the beach beside it.
A west-facing beach a short walk south of town, with hostels and cafés on the road above it.
A south-facing beach, the next one along the coastal path after Kudle.
Smaller south-facing beaches further along the path.
plans: The beach walk from Kudle to Om, Half Moon and Paradise
Sunset at Kudle Beach
Share an auto or taxi from Gokarna Road station
Morning at the Mahabaleshwar Temple and the old town
Day trip to Yana caves
Kayaking or a surf lesson
safety: Strong waves catch swimmers even outside the monsoon. Swim only where lifeguards are on duty, and not after drinking.
Walk the coastal path between beaches in daylight, and with others if you can.
The Mahabaleshwar Temple is an active place of worship, and the UK government's travel advice asks travelers to respect the local dress code at religious sites.
Wear shoes on forest paths after dark; the nearest hospital with snake antivenom is in Kumta, about 25 km away.
tips: Gokarna Road station, on the Konkan Railway, is about 10 km from town, so share an auto or taxi with others off the same train.
Zostel Gokarna is above Main Beach and The Hosteller is about five minutes from Kudle, so either puts you on the coastal path.
Zostel Gokarna lets outsiders into its cafe, so you can meet its guests without staying there.
best: October to March is the dry season; the June to September monsoon brings rough seas.

faq: Which beach in Gokarna should I stay near to meet people?
Main Beach and Kudle. Zostel Gokarna is on the cliff above Main Beach and The Hosteller Gokarna is about five minutes' walk from Kudle, so either puts you close to the beaches and the coastal path.

description: Traveling solo in Bir Billing? Where travelers meet, social hostels, plans to join, the paragliding season and safety tips, plus how to find company.
intro: Bir is a village in Himachal's Kangra district known as India's paragliding capital. Pilots take off from the meadow at Billing, 14 km up the hill, and land at Chowgan on Bir's southern edge, where most of the hostels and cafés are. A Tibetan colony with several monasteries gives you plenty to do on days you don't fly.
areas: Bir's southern edge, where paragliders land and where most guesthouses, hostels and cafés are.
At the west end of Chowgan, with several monasteries, a Tibetan handicraft centre and the Deer Park Institute.
The old village centre, about 20 minutes' walk above the colony.
The take-off meadow at about 2,400 m, 14 km north of Bir.
plans: Share a taxi up to Billing for the take-off or the view
Sunset at the landing site
A slow cafe morning in Chowgan
Walk to Chokling Monastery and its stupa in the Tibetan Colony
Walk to Sherab Ling Monastery, about an hour from Chowgan
Tour the Bir Tea Factory
safety: Fly only with a licensed tandem pilot, booked through a registered operator, and ask to see the licence before you pay.
Paragliding stops for the monsoon, from mid-July to mid-September.
Mountain roads are narrow; avoid driving or riding after dark.
Tell someone your route before hiking alone towards Billing or the waterfalls.
tips: Ahju, a narrow-gauge station on the Pathankot line, is 3 km from Bir; the nearest broad-gauge station is Pathankot, about 112 km from Bir.
McLeod Ganj and Dharamshala are about 50 km away, two to three hours by road, so the two fit one trip.
We'd expect fewer travelers outside the flying season, so in the quiet months a hostel that runs events, or a posted plan, is the easiest way to find company.
best: September and October for flying, with some flying in November. Paragliding stops for the monsoon, from mid-July to mid-September.

meet_spots.name: Billing take-off meadow
meet_spots.why: The launch site, a meadow at about 2,400 m, 14 km north of Bir.

meet_spots.name: Chokling Monastery

meet_spots.why: A centre for the study of classical Indian wisdom traditions in the Tibetan Colony, which hosts frequent guest lectures and workshops.

extra.title: Paragliding safely in Bir
extra.intro: What we could check on 11 October 2026:

items.name: The monsoon ban
items.why: In 2025 the Kangra administration banned all paragliding at Bir Billing, tandem and solo, from 15 July to 15 September, and described the break as a regular annual practice.

items.name: Licensed tandem pilots
items.why: Tandem pilots in Himachal need a licence under the state's Aero Sports Rules, 2022. A 2025 amendment adds a simulation safety course before a tandem licence, and pilots already registered with the Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation had until 31 August 2026 to complete it.

getting_there.name: By road, rail and air
getting_there.why: Bir is off NH 154 between Baijnath and Jogindernagar, about 50 km south-east of Dharamshala. The nearest stations are Ahju (narrow gauge, 3 km) and Pathankot (broad gauge, about 112 km), and Kangra Airport is about 67 km away.

getting_there.name: Group trips from Delhi
getting_there.why: Delhi operators run short group trips here, such as Unite Strangers' 4-day Bir and Palachak trip, listed from 20 November 2026.

faq: Is Bir quiet in the off-season?

We'd expect fewer people outside the flying season, which runs in September and October with some flying in November; paragliding stops for the monsoon, from mid-July to mid-September. In the quieter months, stay at a hostel that runs events, or post a plan on Tablamigo so anyone nearby can join.
Can I paraglide in Bir in the monsoon?
No. Flying stops every monsoon: in 2025 the Kangra administration banned all paragliding at Bir Billing from 15 July to 15 September.
